# Data Construction and Provenance {#sec-app-data}

The paper harmonizes survey, Census, administrative, and economic data to Census-2001 districts. This appendix documents the source timing, lineage rules, schooling constructs, linguistic measures, consumption construction, and other outcome panels used in the public analysis. The purpose is reproducibility rather than additional specification search.

# Identification Diagnostics {#sec-app-identification}

The main paper treats linguistic distance as an inherited opportunity gradient and uses the IV analysis only to define an identification boundary. This appendix records the full forensic case: geographic absorption, controls, scale and influence checks, alternative distance constructions, historical balance and pretrends, historical relevance, monotonicity, richer language vectors, weak-IV dynamics, robustness-family coverage, and exclusion sensitivity.

# Extended Local-Development Outcomes {#sec-app-development}

The main paper reports a deliberately bounded synthesis of the local-development evidence. The full registered outcome families appear here. Census and Economic Census windows that overlap the 2007--08 schooling measure are interpreted as co-evolving development margins, not as identified post-treatment mediators of EMI.

# Selection into Education {#sec-app-selection}

The household-level enrollment model is retained as descriptive evidence that educational participation is socially structured. It is not used as a control function, Heckman correction, propensity-score design, or source of policy instruments in the district-level causal analysis.
